sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: The Act established the **Governor-General of Bengal** (Warren Hastings) and a **Council of Four** to assist him, shifting power from the three presidencies to a centralized authority.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: It mandated the EIC to report on its **Revenue, Civil, and Military affairs** in India to the British Government, establishing the principle of parliamentary oversight.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: It prohibited EIC servants from engaging in **private trade** or accepting **bribes/gifts** from natives to curb corruption.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The Act was a response to the EIC's financial crisis and the need for accountability following the Bengal Famine of 1770.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Centralization**: Subordinated the Presidencies of Bombay and Madras to the Governor-General of Bengal.
• **Accountability**: First time the British Parliament asserted the right to regulate the Company's Indian administration.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: The Governor-General had no veto power over his Council, leading to frequent deadlocks.
• **Solutions**: The Amending Act of 1781 and the Pitt's India Act of 1784 were introduced to rectify these structural flaws.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'G-S-C' (Governor, Supreme Court, Control).
• **Decoded Meaning**: G = Governor-General of Bengal; S = Supreme Court at Calcutta; C = Control of EIC by British Parliament.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: The Act did NOT establish a 'Supreme Court of India' but a 'Supreme Court at Calcutta'. Also, it did not abolish the EIC, but merely regulated it.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Dual Control' or 'Parliamentary Oversight' to describe the shift in the nature of the Company's governance.

keyTakeaways: The Act marked the beginning of British constitutional control over India.
It created the office of Governor-General of Bengal, centralizing power.
It established the Supreme Court at Calcutta to administer English law.
